blockers.title: Normal final reap has no source-level deadline/stop bound
blockers.finding: After NOTE_EXIT and a positive helper receipt, both identical main definitions call os.waitpid(proc.pid,0). Unlike the stop handshake and cleanup reap, this call has no WNOHANG/deadline loop or stop-latch check. The signal handlers append a request rather than raise. A retained process-exit notification is source-design evidence, not an observed guarantee that this blocking call returns inside the reserved whole60-second closure. A future external late-refusal gate does not replace the owner's required bounded cleanup control.
blockers.recommendation: In a new immutable successor only, use exact-PID WNOHANG reaping under the existing original deadline/reserved closure and stop policy; preserve raw status and assign Popen.returncode only after the deliberate successful terminal reap. Do not add a wait allowance, process query, fallback or synthetic exit0.
blockers.scope: Static missing-bound finding, not an observed hang, syscall timing measurement or installed-kernel diagnosis.

blockers.title: Final handled-stop snapshot precedes handler cutoff
blockers.finding: handled_stop_requests copies the latch before restoring SIGCHLD/INT/TERM dispositions. A handled TERM/INT arriving between that copy and restoration is present in controller_stop_requests, so complete_candidate/final return correctly refuse, but it can be absent from the saved handled_stop_requests list. The receipt then loses a known stop observation in the interval it claims to cover.
blockers.recommendation: In the successor, finalize the saved latch after the documented handler restoration/cutoff, retain every request received before that cutoff and record an explicit refusal reason when latched. Preserve the honest post-cutoff default-signal/partial-or-nonzero refusal limit; no all-lifetime signal claim or new signal framework.
blockers.scope: Evidence-retention gap; this does not claim the source accepts a latched stop.

blockers.title: Pre-certificate direct-signal error skips the bounded reap attempt
blockers.finding: The pre-certificate/not-continued os.kill(proc.pid,SIGKILL) and stop-action append share the broad try with the subsequent WNOHANG reap loop. If the own-PID kill raises, including ESRCH, control jumps to the outer except and never attempts the still-required explicit wait on the retained direct child. A signal error does not itself consume or invalidate the known parent-child wait relationship.
blockers.recommendation: Catch and retain the direct-signal error locally, then always attempt the existing bounded exact-PID explicit terminal reap. Keep unknown cleanup/nonzero/permission errors as refusal and do not reinterpret ESRCH from a signal call as completed reap or group absence. Never introduce guessed group cleanup before a valid certificate.
